A quick example: 250 kcal per 100 g.

For a 40 g portion, calculate 250 × 40 ÷ 100 = 100 kcal. These are example inputs to show the arithmetic, not a value for a particular food.

How to estimate a portion from a label.

Keep the energy value and portion weight on the same basis before calculating.

Find the reference value

Read the label or choose a food record. If the value is per 100 g, enter it as shown. A food record describes that food and preparation, not every version of it.

Weigh the portion

Enter the grams for the amount you want to estimate. If you use a label's per-serving value instead, first divide by that serving's gram weight and multiply by 100.

Read the estimate

The calculator multiplies kcal per 100 g by grams and divides by 100. For a recipe, estimate ingredients separately, add them, then divide by equal portions; ingredients left in a pan or uneven portions can change the result.

Questions about calorie estimates.

What if my label shows calories per serving?

Divide the stated calories by the serving's weight in grams, then multiply by 100 to get a per-100 g value. For example, 210 kcal in a 60 g serving is 350 kcal per 100 g. Then enter 350 and the weight of your portion.

Does this calculator identify the food?

No. It only scales the number you provide. To find a reference value by food name, try the QikCal Food Library browser preview.

Are the results exact?

No. The arithmetic follows the inputs, but labels and food records can differ from the food you ate. Ingredients, preparation, recipe, and portion weight all matter.

Does the calculator save what I enter?

No. The calculator runs in your browser and does not save or send your values. The separate iPhone diary is a one-time App Store purchase; it has no in-app free trial.

This tool is for general food reference, not medical or nutrition advice. For guidance about a medical condition, consult your doctor or a qualified healthcare professional.
